name: Shoot / Aim
subtitle: Aiming, hitting, and resource management create a closed loop; the core lies in hit feedback and risk-reward.
demoRuleHint: Rule: Aim → Fire → Hit determination → Feedback (knockback/explosion/score) → Cooldown/Reload
problemsSolved: Turn hit detection and feedback into a learnable rhythmic window (why hitting feels good).
Use constraints like ammo, recoil, and spread to control erratic shots and unlimited output.
Make pressure come from interpretable targets and rhythm, not just monster stacking.
Balancing ammo limits and output: too much ammo leads to overkill and lack of rhythm; too little ammo forces frequent reloading, breaking combo flow.
Balancing recoil and accuracy: excessive recoil makes shooting unstable and reduces combos; weak recoil makes players too precise, diminishing challenge.
Overly precise shooting weakens game rhythm: when players can easily hit all targets, the game loses tension and players may stop actively seeking dodge or strategy.
learningGoals: Understand how hit feedback creates satisfying moments.
Master how fire rate, spread, and recoil shape gameplay difficulty.
Be able to design clear projectile trajectories, hit detection, and occlusion rules.
minimalRules: Hit: ray or projectile detection and occlusion.
systemLoopHint: Input (aim/fire) → Resolution (hit/occlusion) → Feedback (damage/recoil) → Resource change (cooldown/ammo) → New target.

combos.effect: Movement creates windows of opportunity, forming a high-pressure loop.
Accumulate resources through hits/kills to drive weapon progression.
Projectile trajectories interact with the environment, expanding strategic space.

advancedWarnings: Weak hit feedback makes shooting feel like 'air shots'.
Unexplained recoil and spread break the learning curve.
Inconsistent occlusion rules cause strong frustration.
advancedAlgoRefs: Hit detection: rays/projectiles, collision layers, hitboxes.
Spawn generation: enemy refresh rhythm and wave design.
